title: Fenrir Claw
text: Wolf crumpled to the ground with a thud. Oh? Was he about to lose? Wolf tried to get back up as though his legs had given out beneath him, but couldn't quite manage it, and turned his gaze toward Phantom Wolf, then toward Father. Then... after squeezing his eyes shut tight, he snapped them open, sprang back to his feet, and lunged at Phantom Wolf.
“Vauuuuu!”
“Gaaaaaaaa!”
With a whoosh, Phantom Wolf countered using that same shadow-like afterimage movement it had used to dodge Brionac earlier—but somehow, Wolf produced an afterimage too, indeed.
“Ooh... he can copy that?”
“Can he actually learn it? He dodged Spear Hero’s attack in one shot, after all.”
“This is turning into something we shouldn’t underestimate.”
Father, Rabbit Guy, and Crocodile Guy all let out cries of admiration at how Wolf had dodged Phantom Wolf’s technique.
“Structurally, it looks like some kind of illusion-type skill, but...”
“I wonder just what kind of mechanism lets him dodge like that?”

Panda and Elephant tilted their heads too, puzzled. Somehow it felt to me like the sort of movement you’d see while playing around with Filolial-sama folk. I suspected it was some kind of speed-boosting technique.
“Gauuuu!”
“Vofuuuuuu!”

Phantom Wolf cloaked itself in darkness and charged, while Wolf, in contrast, let out a light that seemed like some kind of ki energy and charged in just the same. It was basically an aura tackle, I’d say. The two collided with crackling force, sending shockwaves through the surrounding area. Then, in one especially flashy clash, their energies collided and exploded.
“Vau!”
And then I saw it clearly: Wolf, overpowering Phantom Wolf, slammed his fist straight into its face.
“Gyan!”
Sent flying, Phantom Wolf crashed to the ground spread-eagled. Then it began to give off a faint glow.
“Haah... haah... haah... Vof.”
“...Haah.”
Wolf, standing there out of breath, raised a fist. Then the fallen wolf-man that was Phantom Wolf slowly rose up, rubbing the spot where he’d been struck as he got to his feet.
“Ow... that one landed. Not bad at all, Magarum.”

It spoke! And that’s when it hit me... this wolf-man Phantom Wolf, despite the different coloring, looked an awful lot like the Claw Hero that Takt’s fox-pig had transformed into... though honestly, it was all pretty hazy to me. I only sort of sensed that must be the general gist of things from the mood in the air, indeed. Father and the others were certainly giving off that kind of vibe, after all.
“V-Vof...”

“Haha, nah... next thing I knew, you were right there in front of me and we were fighting. You look different now, but I could tell it was you, Magarum. Man, that was a fun fight. And you’ve turned out way better than I expected, too.”
Phantom Wolf’s wolf-man form glanced around at his surroundings, still wrapped in that faint glow.
“What in the world’s going on here... The way I remember it, I figured I was off training in the mountains somewhere. Guess that ain’t quite it, huh.”
“Heh, I see you’ve picked up some weird verbal tic there, Magarum. Guess I’m not exactly alive anymore, am I.”
Wolf gave a small nod to the wolf-man.
“...Brother. I... back then, I was so scared my legs gave out, and I couldn’t do anything... I just watched you get killed so pathetically, and in the end...”
As though confessing to himself, Wolf murmured his regrets to his ghostly brother.
“Huh? What good’s worrying about that gonna do? Look how strong you’ve gotten since then.”
“Wow... he’s exactly as boisterous as he looks.”
At Father’s murmur, the ghostly wolf-man turned to face him.
“Looks to me like you’re the one they call Shield Hero-sama, the answer to Siltvelt’s long-cherished wish. Seems you’ve made quite the fine man out of my little brother—much obliged!”
“Ah, yes. I’ve been looking after him in various ways.”
“Hahaha! Feel free to put him to good use. He’s a bit of a sly one, but he’s not a bad kid at heart. I always figured if he was raised right he’d surpass me, but this is even beyond what I imagined.”
“Gahahahaha!” The wolf-man who seemed to be Wolf’s older brother laughed heartily. Then, gradually, his expression turned serious, and he pierced Wolf with a sharp, glaring gaze.

“I can feel it, coming through this Claw Seven Star Weapon. Quit moping around forever, would you? I don’t hold anything against you, and I don’t think you’re pathetic either. Keep your heart strong. And don’t you dare fight just to make up for some imagined sin, you hear?”
“Brother... I, I...”
Just as Wolf began to break down in tears, his brother—ghost though he was—punched him.
“That’s what I’m saying, don’t you go crying on me! C’mon! You’ve still got things left to do, don’t you? As long as you’re alive, the fight keeps going! Keep fighting for the thing you really want!”
“V-Vof... I—I understand! I’ll... do my best! I’ll give it everything, so...!”
“Damn right!”
Just as he said that, as though something were unraveling, the figure of the wolf-man who resembled Wolf’s brother began to grow hazy and fade.
“Guess I don’t have much time left. Well, the Claw Seven Star Weapon can finally rest easy now, huh? Give it your all!”
“Vofuuuuu!”
“Waoooooo—”

As the two howled together, the figure of the wolf-man resembling Wolf’s brother vanished, and the Claw Seven Star Weapon returned to being one again, glinting brightly. Its shape had changed somehow—now it looked like a claw shaped like a wolf’s head. Somehow, it felt familiar.
“Vof? Fenrir Claw?”
“Ah, right, you mentioned Fenrir the other day. So that’s the kind of claw that came out of it?”
“Voff. And I can tell the claw’s attack power itself has gotten stronger! I can put out even more power now!”
“Well, looks like whatever was weighing on you got sorted out, Wolf. So, how was it, getting to talk with your brother?”
“Vof... I was being so stupid, worrying like that. It was ridiculous.”
“Haha...” Father gave a dry laugh at Wolf’s words.
“He really had that bold, boisterous energy, huh.”
“And besides... I can feel power surging up from deep within my body... Vofuuuuu!”
The moment Wolf raised his voice like that, he transformed from his wolf-man form into an even bigger, silver-furred wolf.
“Oh... shifting from Demi-Human form into full beast form.”
“Waooooon! Power’s surging through me. I can fight even harder now!”
With that, Wolf lowered his head to Father and offered a Siltvelt-style salute.
“Great Shield Hero-sama, I apologize for showing you such an unsightly display. I humbly ask for your continued guidance going forward. Vof.”
“Sure. Let’s keep at it together.”
“Vof! I’ll do my best!”
And so, somehow, Father and Wolf had wrapped things up between them.
“Seems like things got sorted out nicely, and he’s gotten a whole lot stronger too... but is there really an enemy out there strong enough to need all that?”
“Don’t even start... With how much the Heroes have been powered up, even that Takt guy got one-shotted. What kind of strong enemy could possibly be left out there?”

“Right? Same goes for Bow Hero—pretty much everything’s been small fry, taken down without any trouble. At this point, the only real challenge left would be taking on the Four Cardinal Heroes and actually winning.”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy were having this exchange in hushed voices.
“Voff, voff, please pet my belly, voff~”
“Ahaha, even all grown up like this, you still come to me for pets, don’t you, Wolf.”
In his wolf form, Wolf lay sprawled out in front of Father, begging to have his belly rubbed. Honestly, act your age already.
“Making a fool of himself again... where exactly am I supposed to find any sign of intelligence in that.”
“Says the one who’s looking at him with pure envy.”
“Guh... I’m aware, thank you.”
Somewhere beneath the grass, your brother’s definitely crying his eyes out at that pathetic display—so quit it already.
“Seriously, things just resolve themselves the moment you watch, huh... Maybe we should’ve just stayed back resting at the castle?”

“Let’s just agree not to say that out loud, shall we. Well, I’ll go ahead and turn it into a poem or something. Good for getting people fired up, right? Though I won’t be recreating that particular scene.”
“Heh. Making it into a play, are we?”
“Call it whatever you like.”
“A poem... right, I suppose. It really is quite the story, isn’t it. Somehow that’s annoying to admit.”
Rabbit Guy seemed to feel some rivalry toward Elephant’s plans.
“Elmelo, is it over? Kou doesn’t really get it.”
“I suppose so. Well, I’ll sum it up nice and simply for you. We’ll be heading back before long.”
“Got it—let’s head home.”

And so, it seemed that whatever had been troubling Wolf was finally resolved, and along with it, his claw—along with his abilities overall—had been dramatically strengthened. Indeed, his movements and the sharpness of his attacks had clearly increased by leaps and bounds.
